relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: In radicular pain models, MaR-1 inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, preventing pain-related cellular processes.

relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: It also inhibits TRPV1 ion channels and suppresses Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release from nociceptors, key steps in pain perception.

relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Maresin-1 has also been reported to dampen dorsal root ganglion neuron activation and inhibit CGRP release

relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Additionally, MaR-1 inhibits NF-κB signaling, reducing transcription of pro-inflammatory genes and inflammation-induced pain.

relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Correlation analysis demonstrated a significant negative association between serum MaR-1 levels and VAS pain (r = −0.759, P < .001), DAS28 (r = −0.683, P < .001) in RA patients.

relationships.subject: Maresin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Serum MaR-1 levels were significantly higher in the control group than in either patient group (P < .001).

key_findings: Serum MaR-1 was lower in RA and FM than healthy controls and inversely correlated with VAS pain (RA r=-0.759; FM r=-0.614) and DAS28 in RA
MaR-1 was lower in RA patients with high disease activity and possible neuropathic pain; ROC AUC 0.94 (RA) and 0.93 (FM)
